title: Przepraszam, gdzie jest…?
title_en: Asking the way in the street
note: Situations/chunk unit — asking for and understanding directions in the street. Fixed phrases, learned whole, no rule slides. Only FOUR genuinely new words: ktoredy, isc, wiem, bardzo. Everything else (prosto, lewo, prawo, w lewo, w prawo, daleko, blisko, przepraszam, prosze, dziekuje, gdzie, jest, czy, to, nie, tak) is already in POOL and is RECYCLED into a new function here. TRAP 1 — 'Jak dojsc do…?' was DROPPED. dojsc is perfective and the standing decision for this batch is imperfective-only, even inside fixed chunks. Replacement: 'Ktoredy do…?' — it has NO VERB IN IT AT ALL, so aspect never arises, and it hangs entirely off do + genitive, which a1_prep_do_z already taught with the exact place-genitives used here (do apteki, do banku, do centrum, do parku, do szpitala). One new word, zero new grammar. TRAP 2a — INFINITIVE QUARANTINE. 'isc' is NOT in POOL (only ide, idziesz are). a2_chodzic owns the full grid and was not read. 'Prosze isc…' is therefore carried as an OPAQUE BLOCK: the form is never named, never called an infinitive, never conjugated, never contrasted with ide or idziesz, and no motion/verb structure id is tagged — situation_chunk only. Every quiz choice touching it is a WHOLE PHRASE; there is no isc/ide/idziesz/idzie four-way anywhere, which would open the grid by the back door. isc is listed in teaches_lemmas so this pack stands on its own feet and depends on nothing being written in parallel. TRAP 2b — ORDINALS DROPPED ENTIRELY. 'pierwsza' is not in POOL and ordinals belong to a2_ordinals_time. No 'pierwsza ulica', no ordinal anywhere, and 'ulicy' (locative) is avoided too — it is untaught. The 'take the first street on the left' function is simply not offered; 'Prosze isc w lewo' does the same job with taught material. SECOND QUARANTINE — 'Nie wiem.' is taught as one street phrase. znac/znam IS already taught, so the wiedziec-vs-znac split is live ground; this unit NEVER mentions znam, never conjugates wiem, and never shows the infinitive. Only wiem and nie wiem are tagged. Real contrast the unit DOES teach, because both cases are already taught: Gdzie jest apteka? (nominative, plain dictionary form) vs Ktoredy do apteki? (genitive, the same do apteki he already has). 'potem', 'tedy', 'skrzyzowanie', 'rog', 'toaleta', 'muzeum' were all checked against POOL, found absent, and left out for restraint.

intro.title: Przepraszam, gdzie jest…? — start every question with these three words
intro.body:
You already own every word in this question. Przepraszam gets a stranger's attention, gdzie means where, jest means is. Put the name of the place on the end and you have asked your first question in a Polish street.

The place keeps its plain dictionary form here — exactly as it looks in a word list. Nothing is added to it: apteka, hotel, bank, przystanek, dworzec.

Say Przepraszam first and pause. It is the difference between a question and a demand.
intro.body_pl: Przepraszam, gdzie jest apteka? Gdzie jest hotel? Gdzie jest przystanek?

rows: Excuse me, where is the chemist's?

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the post office?

intro.title: Którędy do…? — asking for the way, not the place
intro.body:
Którędy means which way. It is the one new word on this slide and it does a job Gdzie jest…? cannot: it asks for the route, not the location.

What follows it is the do you have had since A1 — do apteki, do banku, do parku, do centrum. After do the place takes the genitive, and these are the very phrases you already practised.

So the two questions pull the noun in opposite directions, and it is worth ten seconds:
Gdzie jest apteka? — plain form.
Którędy do apteki? — genitive, because of do.

Notice there is no verb anywhere in Którędy do…?. That is why it is the easiest way to ask how to get somewhere.
intro.body_pl: Którędy do apteki? Którędy do centrum? Którędy do parku?

examples.en: Excuse me, which way to the chemist's?

intro.title: The answer you will hear — prosto, w lewo, w prawo
intro.title_pl: Proszę iść prosto. Proszę iść w lewo. Proszę iść w prawo.
intro.body:
Proszę iść… is the polite "Please go…" that Poles use to give directions to a stranger.

Take these three whole. Proszę you already know, and prosto, w lewo and w prawo are already yours as well. The middle word is the only new thing, and this unit asks you to leave it exactly as it stands — its family is a later unit and you lose nothing by not opening it now. Say the phrase whole and it is always right.

In practice you will often hear just the last part on its own: Prosto. W lewo. W prawo. That is a complete answer in the street.
intro.body_pl: Proszę iść prosto. Proszę iść w lewo. Proszę iść w prawo. Prosto. W lewo. W prawo.

rows: a whole answer on its own

intro.title: Czy to daleko? · To blisko. — the second question you will always want
intro.body:
Nothing new here at all. Czy turns anything into a yes/no question, to means it, and daleko and blisko are words you already have.

Czy to daleko? = Is it far?
To blisko. = It's near.
To daleko. = It's far.

Ask it straight after you have been given the way. If the answer is To daleko, you now know to look for a bus stop rather than start walking.
intro.body_pl: Czy to daleko? To blisko. To daleko.

rows: the answer you are hoping for

intro.title: Nie wiem. · Dziękuję bardzo. — closing the exchange either way
intro.body:
Two last phrases and the street is survivable.

Nie wiem = I don't know. This is the everyday answer when a stranger asks you something and you have no idea — and it is also, often, what you will hear back. Learn it whole; wiem is not a word to take apart at this stage.

Bardzo means very, or a lot. Dziękuję bardzo = thank you very much, and it is what you say the moment someone has pointed you the right way.

Bardzo also strengthens the words you already have, and it goes in front of them: To bardzo blisko. To bardzo daleko.
intro.body_pl: Nie wiem. Dziękuję bardzo. To bardzo blisko. To bardzo daleko.

quiz.prompt: Excuse me, where is the chemist's? →
quiz.explain: After Gdzie jest the place keeps its plain dictionary form. It is do that pulls the genitive, and there is no do in this question.

quiz.prompt: Where is the bank?  →  Gdzie jest ___?
quiz.explain: W banku says you are inside it and do banku says you are heading there. Gdzie jest only asks where it stands, so the word stays as the dictionary has it.

quiz.prompt: You want to know the way to the park. →
quiz.explain: Do always pulls the genitive — the same do parku you already know. Drop the do and the question falls apart.
Gdzie jest centrum? asks where it is. Którędy asks for the route to it — which way you should walk.
Prosto is straight on. The frame in front of it never changes — only the last word does.
Którędy asks for the way, so the answer has to be a direction. Czy to daleko? would be answering a question with a question.
Czy at the front is what makes it a yes/no question. Without it, To daleko is a statement — it's far.
The other three contradict themselves: nie then daleko, or tak then blisko. Match the yes or no to what follows it.

quiz.prompt: Someone asks you the way and you have no idea. You say:
quiz.explain: Nie wiem is one fixed phrase for I don't know. Nie, to blisko would be answering a different question altogether.

quiz.prompt: Someone has just shown you the way. You say:
quiz.explain: Przepraszam opens the exchange and Dziękuję bardzo closes it. Say them in that order and the whole thing works.
Bardzo stands directly in front of the word it strengthens, exactly as very does in English.
